u10_statues: Unit 10, Page 99, Culture, Exercise 2
Statues
There are many wonderful statues all over the world.
Many of them help us to remember the lives of great people.
Rosa Parks
One day in 1965, a bus driver in Alabama in the US asked Rosa Parks to give a man her seat because he was white and she was black.
She said no and the police decided to take her away.
It was a very important moment in the history of black people's rights in the US.
The statue shows Rosa sitting on a rock wearing the same clothes as that day in 1965.
Franz Kafka
Franz Kafka was a writer from Prague.
He was born in 1883.
His books were in German.
In his life, he was not very famous, but now he is.
Many of his stories were very strange.
There's a very unusual statue of him in Prague.
He's sitting on the shoulders of an empty suit.
Os Candango
The Candango were men who travelled from all over Brazil between 1956 and 1960 to build the new capital city of Brazil, Brasilia.
In 1956, 256 men arrived, but before long there were 30,000 who worked hard to build the city.
Brasilia opened in 1960 and this 8 meter high statue to remember the Candango is in the 3 powers square.
The two figures are holding digging tools.
Suzanne Longlan
At the Roland Garros tennis centre in Paris, there is a court called Suzanne Longlan.
Longlan was a famous French tennis player who played from 1914 to 1926.
She was the number one player for many years.
In front of the court is this statue.
Longlan is jumping with a racket in her hand and she is wearing her famous white dress and headband.
u11_dolphins: Unit 11, page 102, reading, exercise 3.
Dolphins to the Rescue
Everyone knows that dolphins are very intelligent animals.
But did you know that many scientists believe there is a special connection between dolphins
and humans?
There are lots of stories about dolphins helping humans who are in danger.
Here are two of our favourites.
14-year-old Davide Cedci was in his father's boat off the southeast coast of Italy when
he had an accident and fell into the water.
Davide didn't know how to swim, and his father didn't see him fall, so he didn't stop
the boat.
He shouted, but his dad didn't hear him.
Davide got very worried.
Then, very quickly, a dolphin came to help him.
It gave Davide a push back up to the top of the water, and the boy got on to the dolphin's
back.
The dolphin took him back to the boat.
When Davide's father saw his son, he pulled him from the water.
The dolphin saved Davide's life.
In 2016, Adam Walker went to New Zealand to swim across the Cook Strait between the North
and South Islands.
He was swimming when he saw a large dark shape below him.
He knew that it was a great white shark and his life was in danger.
Adam knew he didn't have a lot of time.
A few seconds later, a group of ten dolphins joined him and swam in a circle between him
and the shark.
The circle of dolphins kept Adam safe.
After half an hour, the shark left, but the dolphins swam with him for another hour.
u11_extinct: Unit 11, page 106. Reading. Exercise 2.
Extinct Animals
1. The Great Ork
The Great Ork was a large seabird that lived in the North Atlantic. It was a bird but it
couldn't fly. It could swim underwater really well. It caught and ate fish when it
dived under the water. Its feathers were very soft and people used them to make
pillows for their beds. Because of this people killed the birds. The last Great
Ork died on the island of Eldy in 1835.
2. The Tasmanian Tiger
The Tasmanian Tiger was only found in Australia, Tasmania and New Guinea. It
got its name because it had stripes like a tiger but it was not a member of the
cat family. Farmers believed Tasmanian Tigers killed their sheep so they paid
people to kill them. Many of the tigers died after getting ill from diseases they
caught from other animals. The last Tasmanian Tiger died in Hobart Zoo in 1936.
3. Stellar Sea Cow
Stellar Sea Cow was a large animal that lived in the cold Arctic waters around Alaska.
It grew up to nine metres long. Because it was so big it couldn't go under the
water. It ate the plants on top of the sea. It wasn't a very dangerous animal.
It was quite friendly. Because of this it was very easy to kill. Europeans first
found the sea cow in 1741. 27 years later they killed the last one.
